_comment: Grade 1 Unit 2 (What kind of garden would be best?) exercises only 7 of Stage 1's 18 Cambridge sub-strands as extracted from the source pack. These three additions close Recording findings (1Rf), Evaluating sources (1Es) and Cooperation and interdependence (1Cc) with new Activity Sheet pages in Karim's own voice, matching the unit's existing style and its model-garden group project. Added 2026-09-17 to close a documented coverage gap.

addExplainers.title: Our garden vote
addExplainers.body:
Ask your family or your classmates one question: which would you like most in a garden — flowers, vegetables, or a tree?

For every person who says flowers, draw one flower. For every person who says vegetables, draw one vegetable. For every person who says a tree, draw one tree.

Count your drawings. Which one has the most?
bullets: Draw one picture for every answer.
Count and say which got the most votes.

addExplainers.title: Choosing a good picture about gardens
addExplainers.body:
Your grown-up will show you two pictures: one of a real garden, and one of something else, like a car.

Which picture helps you learn about gardens? Point to it, and say why.

A good source is one that really helps you learn about your topic. A picture of a car does not help you learn about gardens, even if it is a nice picture.
bullets: Point to the one that helps you learn about gardens.

addExplainers.title: Sharing our garden tools
addExplainers.body:
When you make your model garden with a partner, you will only have one pot of glue and one box of crayons between you.

Take turns. Pass the glue when your partner needs it. Share the crayons so you both get a turn with your favourite colour.

Afterwards, talk about it: did sharing help you finish your model garden together?
bullets: Share the glue and the crayons with your partner.
Take turns, and wait when it is not your turn.
Say whether sharing helped you finish together.
